# Standalone AI & Programmatic API Specification (`api/API.md`)

Authoritative specification for the standalone authenticated FastAPI service under `/api/` (`api/`), designed for AI agents and programmatic clients while the browser IDE runs separately under `/webapi/` (`webapp/API.md`).

## 1. Architectural Overview & Reverse-Proxy Routing

The `api/` package provides a read-only-by-default, token-efficient REST and MCP service independent of the browser-facing `webapp/` server:

- **Process separation**: `api/main.py` runs on its own port (`127.0.0.1:8001` by default) via `python3 api/main.py` or `uvicorn api.main:app`, while `webapp/main.py` serves the browser IDE and `/webapi/*` on port `8000`.
- **Anubis reverse-proxy split**: External bot/AI protection (Anubis) sits in front of `webapp` (`/`, `/b/*`, `/webapi/*` -> port `8000`) and bypasses `/api/*` straight to port `8001`, where `api/security.py` enforces API key authentication, progressive IP lockout, and sliding-window rate limiting on every request.
- **Zero unauthenticated surface**: FastAPI interactive docs are disabled (`docs_url=None`, `redoc_url=None`), OpenAPI schema discovery lives behind auth at `GET /api/openapi.json`, and `CORSMiddleware` is omitted so browser cross-origin preflights or wildcard `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` headers are never emitted.
- **Modular router layout (`api/routers/`)**: `api/routers/v1.py` aggregates focused domain sub-routers under `/api/v1`: `common.py` (shared service singletons, limits, `_ENDPOINT_CATALOG`, path/identifier/offset validators, and `_with_repo`), `code.py` (discovery, repos, branches/tags, versions, filesystem, symbols, pahole, callgraph, and grep), `history.py` (commits, blame, file/symbol/line-range history), `diffs.py` (revision, blob, Kconfig, Kernel API, and man-pages diffs), `kconfig.py` (Kconfig search, symbol detail, build conditions, evaluator, graph, solver, defconfigs, history, and Kbuild objects), `kapi.py` (Kernel API summary, syscalls, exports, params, tracepoints, modules, and device tables/matching), `mail.py` (LKML search, message, thread/versions, and merged commits), `insights.py` (stable backport gaps, subsystem health, release CVE report, and watch change checks), `misc.py` (maintainers, docs, man pages, CVEs, and REST-only utilities), and `nodemap.py` (NodeMap inspection and canvas authoring).
- **MCP server**: `POST /api/mcp` (Streamable HTTP) and `api/mcp_stdio.py` (local stdio) expose every curated `GET /api/v1/*` endpoint (except P3 REST-only utilities marked `mcp=False`), stateless read-only `POST` tools (`POST /api/v1/nodemap/preview`, `POST /api/v1/maintainers/match`, `POST /api/v1/watch/changes`), and (when `api.allow_writes` and caller key scopes permit) programmatic NodeMap canvas authoring endpoints as Model Context Protocol tools through one shared dispatcher (`api/mcp.py`, §5).
- **Service, DB & Canvas separation**: Endpoints in `api/routers/` reuse `webapp/backend/services/*`, `webapp/backend/database/pool.py` (`with get_reader() as reader:`), `webapp/backend/config.py` (`RepoContextMiddleware` and `require_feature`), and `webapp/backend/security/` (`jail.py`, `git.py`, `sql.py`). All database access stays strictly read-only through `db_engine`; `webapp` and `api` `cache_engine` instances remain independent, and persisted NodeMap canvases are stored as atomic JSON files under `api.nodemap_canvas_dir` without SQLite.

## 2. Configuration & CLI Execution

Settings live under the `"api"` section of `config.json` (`core/config.py`, `config.example.json`), resolved with precedence `CLI Flags > Environment Variables > config.json > Built-in Defaults`:

| Key | Default | Env Var | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `host` | `"127.0.0.1"` | `API_HOST` | Bind address for `api/main.py` |
| `port` | `8001` | `API_PORT` | Listen port (`1`–`65535`) |
| `reload` | `false` | `API_RELOAD` | Auto-reload toggle for uvicorn |
| `default_version` | `"v3.0"` (fallback) | `API_DEFAULT_VERSION` | Default revision when `version` is omitted; resolves to the latest indexed mainline release of the active repository (`resolve_default_version()`) unless explicitly pinned in config or env |
| `allow_writes` | `false` | `API_ALLOW_WRITES` / `KIP_API_ALLOW_WRITES` | Master toggle enabling write-scoped endpoints (`nodemap:write`); default `false` keeps the API and MCP strictly read-only (`mcp_stdio.py --allow-writes` overrides env/config for that stdio session via `set_allow_writes_override()`) |
| `nodemap_canvas_dir` | `""` | `API_NODEMAP_CANVAS_DIR` / `KIP_NODEMAP_CANVAS_DIR` | Persistent directory for atomic JSON NodeMap canvas files (defaults to `<config_or_project_dir>/nodemap-canvases`, shared by `api` and `webapp`) |
| `keys` | `[]` | `API_KEYS` / `KIP_API_KEYS` | List of non-empty strings, `{name: key}` mapping, or `{name: {"key": secret, "scopes": [...]}}` scoped mapping (`VALID_API_SCOPES = {"read", "nodemap:write", "write"}`; empty fails closed) |
| `rate_limit.max_requests` | `120` | — | Maximum authenticated requests per `window_seconds` per key and per IP |
| `rate_limit.window_seconds` | `60` | — | Sliding-window duration in seconds |
| `auth_lockout.max_failures` | `5` | — | Missing or invalid key attempts within `failure_window_seconds` before lockout |
| `auth_lockout.failure_window_seconds` | `60` | — | Sliding failure counting window in seconds |
| `auth_lockout.base_lockout_seconds` | `30` | — | Initial temporary ban duration in seconds (doubles each consecutive lockout) |
| `auth_lockout.max_lockout_seconds` | `3600` | — | Maximum progressive lockout duration cap in seconds |
| `trusted_proxies` | `["127.0.0.1", "::1"]` | `API_TRUSTED_PROXIES` | Trusted proxy IPs or CIDRs allowed to supply `client_ip_header` |
| `client_ip_header` | `"X-Forwarded-For"` | `API_CLIENT_IP_HEADER` | Header read when direct peer IP is in `trusted_proxies`: `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Real-IP`, or `CF-Connecting-IP` (case-insensitive; any other value normalizes to `X-Forwarded-For`, `normalize_api_client_ip_header()`) |
| `oauth.enabled` | `false` | `API_OAUTH_ENABLED` / `KIP_API_OAUTH_ENABLED` | Opt-in toggle enabling the built-in MCP OAuth 2.1 authorization server (`/.well-known/oauth-*`, `/.well-known/openid-configuration`, `/api/oauth/*`); when `false`, all OAuth endpoints return `404` |
| `oauth.issuer` | `""` | `API_OAUTH_ISSUER` / `KIP_API_OAUTH_ISSUER` | Public HTTPS base URL (e.g. `"https://kernelinfo.org"`); when empty, derived from `X-Forwarded-Proto` + `X-Forwarded-Host`/`Host` for trusted proxies or the request base URL |
| `oauth.signing_secret` | `""` | `API_OAUTH_SIGNING_SECRET` / `KIP_API_OAUTH_SIGNING_SECRET` | HMAC-SHA256 signing key for access tokens and consent CSRF tokens; when empty and OAuth is enabled, auto-generated (32 random bytes) and persisted atomically to `<oauth_data_dir>/signing_secret.json` (`0600`) |
| `oauth.data_dir` | `""` | `API_OAUTH_DATA_DIR` / `KIP_API_OAUTH_DATA_DIR` | Persistent directory outside `cache_engine` for OAuth state (`signing_secret.json`, `clients/<id>.json`, `auth_codes.json`, `refresh_tokens.json`), defaulting to `<config_or_project_dir>/oauth-data` (`get_oauth_data_dir()`) |
| `oauth.access_token_ttl` | `3600` | `API_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL` / `KIP_API_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL` | Signed access token lifetime in seconds |
| `oauth.refresh_token_ttl` | `2592000` | `API_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL` / `KIP_API_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL` | Opaque refresh token lifetime in seconds (30 days) |
| `oauth.auth_code_ttl` | `120` | `API_OAUTH_AUTH_CODE_TTL` / `KIP_API_OAUTH_AUTH_CODE_TTL` | Single-use authorization code lifetime in seconds |
| `oauth.allow_dcr` | `true` | `API_OAUTH_ALLOW_DCR` / `KIP_API_OAUTH_ALLOW_DCR` | Enable RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration (`POST /api/oauth/register`) when `oauth.enabled` is `true` |
| `oauth.allow_cimd` | `true` | `API_OAUTH_ALLOW_CIMD` / `KIP_API_OAUTH_ALLOW_CIMD` | Enable MCP Client ID Metadata Documents (HTTPS URL `client_id`s) when `oauth.enabled` is `true` |
| `oauth.allowed_redirect_uris` | `DEFAULT_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URIS` | `API_OAUTH_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URIS` / `KIP_API_OAUTH_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URIS` | Allowlist of HTTPS redirect URIs, host/prefix wildcard patterns, custom schemes, and RFC 8252 loopback patterns permitted for DCR and CIMD |
| `oauth.clients` | `[]` | `API_OAUTH_CLIENTS` / `KIP_API_OAUTH_CLIENTS` | Pre-registered static OAuth clients (`client_id`, optional `client_secret`, `name`, `redirect_uris`, optional `max_scopes`, optional `token_endpoint_auth_method`) |

File logging is `logging.api` (`core/config.py`, same keys as `logging.webapp`): `enabled` (`false`), `dir`, `file` (`"api.log"`), `request_mode` (`"all"` or `"errors"`), `error_dir`, `error_file`, `level` (`"INFO"`), overridable by `KIP_API_LOG_ENABLED`, `KIP_API_LOG_DIR`, `KIP_API_LOG_FILE`, `KIP_API_LOG_REQUEST_MODE`, `KIP_API_LOG_ERROR_DIR`, `KIP_API_LOG_ERROR_FILE`, `KIP_API_LOG_LEVEL`. `create_app()` and `api/main.py` call `setup_api_logging()` (`core/logging_setup.py`), which attaches the `api` target exactly like the webapp target (request-mode filter, uvicorn loggers, stdio capture).

A standalone service configuration is `config_api.json` (`API_CONFIG_FILENAME`, `get_service_config_path("api")`). `ensure_standalone_config("api")` seeds it once from `config.json` through `prune_api_config()`, which keeps only `database` (with `ssh_tunnel`), `cache`, `workspace`, `repositories` (without parser `preparse` rules), `api`, and `logging.api`, and sets `api.reload = false`.

CLI entrypoint (`api/main.py`):

```bash
python3 api/main.py [-c config.json] [--host 127.0.0.1] [--port 8001] [--reload | --no-reload]
uvicorn api.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001
python3 api/mcp_stdio.py [-c config.json] [--repo NAME] [--allow-writes]   # local MCP stdio transport (§5.4)
```

`-c` goes through `apply_config_file()` (`api/config.py`): it exports `CONFIG_FILE` / `KERNELINFO_CONFIG` and calls `init_config()`; a missing file is an error.

## 3. Authentication, Anti-Brute-Force Lockout & Rate Limiting

`api/security.py` implements pure ASGI middleware (`ApiAuthMiddleware` and `ApiRequestLoggingMiddleware`) without `BaseHTTPMiddleware` so `ContextVar` repository and key-scope state propagate to sync and async handlers:

1. **Trusted proxy client IP extraction (`extract_client_ip`)**:
   - Forwarding headers are honored only when `scope["client"][0]` belongs to `api.trusted_proxies`; untrusted peers always resolve to their direct socket IP.
   - For `X-Forwarded-For`, hops are walked right-to-left skipping `trusted_proxies`, picking the rightmost untrusted valid IP and falling back to the direct peer IP if malformed.
   - `scope["client_ip"]` is bound immediately before lockout, authentication, and rate-limit checks so `401` and `429` audit logs record the extracted client IP.
2. **Pre-auth IP lockout check**:
   - Evaluated before reading or verifying API keys so locked-out IPs immediately receive `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After` without leaking key validity (blocking even valid keys during the cooldown).
3. **Constant-time API key verification (`verify_api_key_constant_time`), Scoped Keys & Dual OAuth Bearer Auth**:
   - Reads `X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (`extract_presented_credentials()` / `extract_presented_key()`; an empty or whitespace-only `X-API-Key` is treated as absent so it never shadows a valid `Authorization: Bearer` header).
   - Hashes the presented key and every configured `ApiKeyEntry(id, secret, scopes)` with SHA-256 and compares the fixed-length digests with `hmac.compare_digest`, scanning all keys without short-circuiting (neither key length nor match position affects timing) and returning the matched `ApiKeyEntry`.
   - When `api.oauth.enabled` is `true` and an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header does not match a static API key, `ApiAuthMiddleware` verifies the token as an HMAC-SHA256 signed OAuth 2.1 access token (`oauth_manager.verify_access_token()`, §3.1): checking signature, `typ: "kip+at"`, `iss`, `aud`, `exp`, revocation status, and that the backing `sub` key ID still exists in `api.keys`, then intersecting the token's `scope` with the backing key's current scopes and `api.allow_writes`.
   - Plain string list entries and `{id: "secret"}` entries default to `frozenset({"read"})`; scoped objects `{id: {"key": "secret", "scopes": ["read", "nodemap:write"]}}` validate against `VALID_API_SCOPES = frozenset({"read", "nodemap:write", "write"})`.
   - `ApiAuthMiddleware` sets `scope["api_key_id"]` (e.g. `<key_id>` for static keys or `oauth:<sub_key_id>:<client_id>` for OAuth tokens), `scope["api_key_scopes"]`, `_ACTIVE_API_KEY_ID`, and `_ACTIVE_API_SCOPES` inside a `try / finally` block.
   - When `api.oauth.enabled` is `true`, `401` responses include the RFC 9728 challenge header `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="<issuer>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/mcp"` (plus `error="invalid_token"` when a Bearer token was presented and rejected), and `require_write_scope(scope_name="nodemap:write")` attaches `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="<scope_name>", resource_metadata="..."` on HTTP `403` responses.
   - Empty or missing `api.keys` fails closed (`401` on all protected requests).
4. **Failure counting & progressive exponential lockout**:
   - Both missing and invalid API keys/tokens (as well as failed API key submissions on `POST /api/oauth/authorize`) increment the per-IP failure counter and return `401`.
   - Reaching `max_failures` within `failure_window_seconds` triggers a temporary ban of `min(max_lockout_seconds, base_lockout_seconds * 2**(tier - 1))`.
   - Authenticating with a valid key clears the IP's failure streak (`_ip_failures.pop(client_ip, None)`).
   - Tracked IP and key maps are LRU-bounded (`MAX_TRACKED_IPS = 4096`, `MAX_TRACKED_KEYS = 4096`) to prevent memory exhaustion under IP churn.
5. **Authenticated sliding-window rate limits**:
   - Enforced independently per `key_id` and per `client_ip` (`429` + `Retry-After`).
6. **Redacted request logging, security headers & opt-in OAuth CORS**:
   - `SecurityHeadersMiddleware` wraps all responses (including early `401` and `429` rejections, preserving route-level `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and custom `Content-Security-Policy` headers on the OAuth consent page).
   - `ApiRequestLoggingMiddleware` logs via `api.request` using only key names (`key=<name>`), never logging `Authorization`, `X-API-Key`, or raw configured secret values.
   - When `api.oauth.enabled` is `false` (default), zero CORS headers are emitted. When `api.oauth.enabled` is `true` and a request includes an `Origin` header, `ApiAuthMiddleware` answers browser `OPTIONS` preflights with `204 No Content` and attaches `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: WWW-Authenticate, Mcp-Session-Id` so browser-based MCP clients and inspectors can read OAuth discovery challenges.

### 3.1 Built-in OAuth 2.1 Authorization Server (`api/oauth.py`, `api/routers/oauth.py`)

When `api.oauth.enabled` is `true`, `api/app.py` serves a self-contained OAuth 2.1 authorization server conforming to the MCP Authorization Specification while keeping `X-API-Key` and static `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>` authentication active:

- **Discovery & Metadata Endpoints** (exempt from API-key auth when `api.oauth.enabled` is `true`; return `404` when `false`):
  - `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/mcp`, `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/v1` (RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata: `resource`, `authorization_servers: [<issuer>]`, `bearer_methods_supported: ["header"]`, `scopes_supported`).
  - `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/api/mcp`, `GET /.well-known/openid-configuration`, `GET /.well-known/openid-configuration/api/mcp` (RFC 8414 Authorization Server Metadata & OIDC Discovery fallback: `issuer`, `authorization_endpoint`, `token_endpoint`, `revocation_endpoint`, optional `registration_endpoint` when `allow_dcr` is `true`, `code_challenge_methods_supported: ["S256"]`, `client_id_metadata_document_supported`).
- **Client Resolution (`oauth_manager.resolve_client`)**:
  1. **Pre-registered clients (`api.oauth.clients`)**: public PKCE (`token_endpoint_auth_method: "none"`) or confidential (`client_secret_basic` / `client_secret_post` verified via constant-time SHA-256 `hmac.compare_digest`).
  2. **MCP Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD)**: when `allow_cimd` is `true` and `client_id` is an `https://` URL with a non-empty path, `fetch_cimd_document()` resolves DNS via `socket.getaddrinfo()`, blocks loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved/unspecified IPs (`is_public_unicast_ip()`), disables HTTP redirects (`_NoRedirectHandler`), enforces a 5 s timeout and 64 KiB body cap, verifies `doc["client_id"] == client_id` and `token_endpoint_auth_method == "none"`, validates every `redirect_uri` against `api.oauth.allowed_redirect_uris`, and caches the verified `OAuthClient` in an LRU-bounded in-memory cache (`256` entries, `600` s TTL).
  3. **RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration (`POST /api/oauth/register`)**: when `allow_dcr` is `true`, validates `redirect_uris` against `api.oauth.allowed_redirect_uris` (always rejecting `javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`, and non-loopback `http://`), enforces per-IP sliding-window rate limits, persists `<oauth_data_dir>/clients/<client_id>.json` atomically (`0600`, storing only SHA-256 hashes of confidential client secrets), and returns `201 Created`.
- **Authorization & Consent UI (`GET /api/oauth/authorize`, `POST /api/oauth/authorize`)**:
  - Enforces `response_type=code`, mandatory PKCE `code_challenge_method=S256` (rejecting missing PKCE or `plain`), exact or RFC 8252 port-agnostic loopback `redirect_uri` matching (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`), and optional RFC 8707 `resource` validation (`<issuer>`, `<issuer>/api/mcp`, `<issuer>/api/v1`).
  - Renders a self-contained HTML5 consent page with zero external assets, strict `Content-Security-Policy` (`default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'`), `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, HTML-escaped parameters, prominent redirect destination hostname display, an explicit warning banner for loopback redirect URIs, and an HMAC-SHA256 signed CSRF token bound to the authorization request parameters.
  - On `POST`: verifies the CSRF token, authenticates the user-entered server API key via `verify_api_key_constant_time()` (recording failures into `ApiAuthMiddleware`'s progressive IP lockout tracker), caps granted scopes to `requested_scopes ∩ key.scopes ∩ client.max_scopes` (dropping write scopes if `api.allow_writes` is `false`), atomically persists a single-use authorization code (`<oauth_data_dir>/auth_codes.json`), and redirects `302` with `code` and `state` (or `error=access_denied` on Deny).
- **Token Exchange, Refresh Rotation & Revocation (`POST /api/oauth/token`, `POST /api/oauth/revoke`)**:
  - `grant_type=authorization_code`: atomically consumes the single-use code (revoking dependent refresh tokens on replay), verifies client credentials (`client_secret_basic`, `client_secret_post`, or `none`), `redirect_uri`, `resource`, and PKCE `S256` (`code_verifier`), and issues a stateless HMAC-SHA256 access token (`typ: "kip+at"`, `iss`, `sub` = `key.id`, `aud`, `client_id`, `scope`, `iat`, `exp`, `jti`) plus an opaque refresh token (`kip_rt_...`, stored as a SHA-256 hash in `<oauth_data_dir>/refresh_tokens.json`).
  - `grant_type=refresh_token`: atomically rotates the refresh token and re-intersects scopes against the backing API key's current scopes and `api.allow_writes` (immediately failing if the backing API key was removed from `api.keys`).
  - `POST /api/oauth/revoke`: idempotently revokes refresh tokens and access token `jti`s per RFC 7009 (`200 OK`).

## 4. Curated REST API Endpoints (`/api/v1/*`)

All `/api/v1/*` endpoints include `"repo": get_active_repo_name()` in their JSON response, honor `X-KI-Repo` or `?repo=<name>` (`RepoContextMiddleware`), default `version` via `resolve_default_version()` (`api.default_version` when explicitly pinned, otherwise the latest indexed mainline release of the active repository), enforce per-repo feature flags (`require_feature`, where `"kapi"` and `"api"` are aliases for the Kernel API feature), validate inputs (`safe_rev`, `resolve_and_verify_repo_path`, `validate_pathspecs`, `is_valid_identifier`), and include pagination (`limit`, `offset`, `total`) plus `truncated: bool` where responses are bounded:

| Group | Endpoint | Feature | MCP Tool | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Discovery** | `GET /api/openapi.json` | — | — | Authenticated OpenAPI 3 schema |
| **Discovery** | `GET /api/v1/capabilities` | — | `get_capabilities` | Compact service summary, repos, features, limits, `read_only`/`scopes`, session-accurate `mcp.tools` count, and endpoint catalog (`include_endpoints=false` by default on MCP) |
| **Discovery** | `POST /api/mcp` | — | — | MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint (JSON-RPC 2.0, §5) |
| **Repos** | `GET /api/v1/repos` | — | `list_repos` | Configured and auto-detected repositories |
| **Repos** | `GET /api/v1/branches` | — | `list_branches` | Paginated Git branches of active repository |
| **Repos** | `GET /api/v1/branches/tags` | — | `get_branch_tags` | Paginated tags reachable from `branch` or across a branch `source` |
| **Repos** | `GET /api/v1/versions` | — | `list_versions` | Paginated tags and indexed versions (`q`, `indexed_only`, `include_rc`, `order`: `"desc"` newest-first default or `"asc"`) |
| **Repos** | `GET /api/v1/status` | — | `get_repo_status` | Active repository ingestion status |
| **Code** | `GET /api/v1/tree` | — | `get_tree` | Paginated directory listing (`version`, `path`) |
| **Code** | `GET /api/v1/files/search` | — | `search_files` | Fuzzy file path search (`q`, `version`, `offset < 2000`; `/webapi/fs/search` stays clamped to `<= 200`) |
| **Code** | `GET /api/v1/file` | — | `get_file_slice` | Bounded line slice (`path`, `version`, `start_line`, `end_line`, `limit`) |
| **Code** | `GET /api/v1/file/outline` | — | `get_file_outline` | AST/symbol outline (`path`, `version`) |
| **Code** | `GET /api/v1/file/imports` | — | `get_file_imports` | `#include` directives and imported symbols, plus optional `resolve_header` lookup |
| **Code** | `GET /api/v1/file/resolve` | — | `resolve_file_target` | Resolve `#include` header directives (`header`) or `.o` Kbuild object targets (`object`) |
| **Code** | `GET /api/v1/file/references` | — | `get_file_references` | Includers, Kconfig `source`s, docs, and Kbuild rules referencing `path` |
| **Symbols** | `GET /api/v1/symbols/search` | — | `search_symbols` | Symbol definition prefix search (`q`, `version`) |
| **Symbols** | `GET /api/v1/symbols/definition` | — | `get_symbol_definition` | Ranked definition (with optional local scope via `from_file`, `line`, `col`) |
| **Symbols** | `GET /api/v1/symbols/references` | — | `get_symbol_references` | Paginated categorized cross-references (with local scope and `CPPro_include` lookup) |
| **Symbols** | `GET /api/v1/symbols/hover` | — | `get_symbol_hover` | Hover signature, location, and kernel-doc (with graceful local-scope fallback) |
| **Symbols** | `GET /api/v1/symbols/scope` | — | `get_symbol_scope` | Local variable, parameter, static, or struct-member scope resolution at `path:line:col` |
| **Symbols** | `GET /api/v1/symbols/ast/{ast_id}` | — | `get_symbol_ast` | Recursive AST container subtree (`depth`) |

`GET /api/v1/kconfig/eval` loads the configuration `make ARCH=<arch> <defconfig>` writes (`load_config()` + `set_all_new_symbols("default")`, `parser/kconfig_ast/KCONFIG_API.md` §8.3), applies each `assign` with kconfig's setter rules (`set_value()`; refused or undefined names are listed in `rejected`), and returns `symbols` (`{value, type, defined, visible, changeable}` per name) and `files` (each path's Kbuild condition `expr` with its tristate `result`: `"y"`, `"m"`, `"n"`, or `"?"`, `parser/kbuild_conditions.py` `evaluate()`). Limits: 128 symbols, 64 paths, 128 assignments.

Saved NodeMap canvases (`webapp/backend/services/nodemap_canvas_service.py`, `nodemap_canvas_schema.py`, `nodemap_canvas_layout.py`) conform to the canonical `canvas_model.js` contract (`schema: "kip-nodemap-canvas"`, `version: 1`, all 17 `NODE_TYPES`, `SIZE_LIMITS`, `LOCK_KINDS`, `EDGE_PRESETS`, sub-canvases up to depth 8, and `tours`) and are written atomically (`tempfile.mkstemp` + `os.replace`) to `<nodemap_canvas_dir>/<safe_repo>/<canvas_id>.json` (`/^[\w-]{1,64}$/`).

Nested NodeMaps: node type `nodemap` (`data.canvasId`, `^[\w-]{1,64}$`) references another saved canvas of the same repository; the child document is never embedded. Every write (`create`, `replace`, `ops`, `expand`, `layout`, `nested`, `group`) is rejected with `422` for a newly added reference to a missing canvas and for any reference cycle (including self-references, `a -> b -> a`); edges attach to a nested node as a whole, so `fromField`/`toField` on a `nodemap` endpoint is `422` (strict validation of `nodes`/`edges` payloads reports it before the service runs). `GET /nodemap/canvases/{canvas_id}` and every write result carry `nested_maps` (`{canvasId: card}`) with `status` (`ok` / `missing`), `name`, `version`, `revision`, `counts` (`nodes`, `edges`, `nested`), a geometry `preview`, and `webapp_url`; a deleted child reads as `status: "missing"` and `DELETE` returns `referenced_by`. `GET .../hierarchy` returns the reference tree (`status` `ok` / `missing` / `cycle`), `parents`, `ancestors`, and `invalid_targets`. `POST .../nested` and `POST .../group` accept `expected_revision` (`409` on conflict) and return the new `node_id`, `target_id`, and the updated `parent` envelope (`group` also `moved_node_ids`, `moved_edge_ids`, `rewired_edge_ids`, and the `child` summary).

P3 utilities (`GET /api/v1/compile_commands`, `GET /api/v1/treemap`, and `POST /api/v1/checkpatch`) are registered in `_ENDPOINT_CATALOG` with `"mcp": False`: they are available over REST and advertised in `/api/v1/capabilities` as REST-only, but strictly excluded from MCP `TOOLS`, omitted from `tools/list`, and rejected with `-32602` (`INVALID_PARAMS`) on `tools/call`.

Intentionally unexposed on `/api/v1/*` and MCP: stateful in-memory patch application (`POST /webapi/mail/apply`, `GET /webapi/mail/apply/{id}/file`), interactive browser patch formatting (`POST /webapi/version/{v}/patch/series`, `POST /webapi/version/{v}/patch/format`), Kconfig-evaluated build treemap (`POST /webapi/version/{v}/treemap/build`), and raw binary/image asset streaming (`GET /webapi/fs/raw/{v}`).

---

## 5. MCP Server (`/api/mcp`, `api/mcp_stdio.py`)

`api/mcp.py` implements the Model Context Protocol (JSON-RPC 2.0) directly on FastAPI/Starlette and the standard library (no MCP SDK). The server offers tools only: no resources, prompts, sampling, logging, or completion.

### 5.1 Protocol & Methods

- **Dispatcher**: `handle_message()` (one message), `handle_payload()` (message or batch), and `handle_raw()` (JSON text; `-32700` when malformed) are transport-agnostic and shared by both transports.
- **Protocol versions**: `SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS = ("2025-11-25", "2025-06-18", "2025-03-26", "2024-11-05")`. `initialize` echoes a supported `protocolVersion` and answers any other (or a missing) one with the latest; a non-string `protocolVersion` is `-32602`. The result carries `capabilities: {"tools": {"listChanged": false}}`, `serverInfo` (`name: "kernelinfo-parser"`, `title`, `version: "1.0.0"`), and short `instructions`.
- **Methods**: `initialize`, `ping` (`{}`), `tools/list` (all tools visible to the caller in one page; a non-empty `cursor` is `-32602`), and `tools/call`. Every other method is `-32601`.
- **Notifications** (messages without `id`, e.g. `notifications/initialized`, `notifications/cancelled`, `notifications/progress`) are accepted and never answered or executed. Client responses (`result` / `error` with an `id`) are ignored.
- **Stateless**: no initialization gate, no `Mcp-Session-Id`, no server-to-client requests; each message is independent.
- **Envelope errors**: a non-object message, `jsonrpc` other than `"2.0"`, missing or non-string `method`, `params` that is not an object, or an `id` that is `null`, boolean, or fractional is `-32600`; by-position `params` arrays are `-32602`; dispatcher failures are `-32603` (`"Internal error"`, details only in the server log).
- **Batches**: JSON-RPC arrays of at most `MAX_BATCH_SIZE = 16` messages holding at most one `tools/call` (one HTTP request, one rate-limit hit, runs at most one tool) answer with an array of the non-notification responses; an empty or oversized batch, or one with several `tools/call`s, is `-32600`.
- **Parse errors**: malformed JSON, invalid UTF-8, and nesting deep enough to exhaust the decoder are `-32700`.

### 5.2 Tool Registry & Error Semantics

- **Derivation**: `build_tool_registry()` builds `TOOLS` from the `api/routers/v1.py` `GET` routes (except entries marked `"mcp": False` in `_ENDPOINT_CATALOG`) plus explicitly marked `POST`/`PUT`/`DELETE` routes (`"mcp": True` or write-scoped) in `_ENDPOINT_CATALOG`, one tool per handler in route order. The tool name is the handler name (`get_capabilities`, `list_repos`, `get_branch_tags`, `get_file_slice`, `resolve_file_target`, `compare_struct_layout`, `get_struct_history`, `get_symbol_history`, `get_line_range_commits`, `get_blob_diff`, `get_kconfig_diff`, `get_kapi_diff`, `get_man_diff`, `get_kconfig_graph`, `solve_kconfig_symbol`, `lookup_kconfig_defconfigs`, `get_kconfig_symbol_history`, `lookup_kbuild_objects`, `get_kapi_summary`, `list_kapi_syscalls`, `lookup_kapi_exports`, `list_kapi_params`, `lookup_kapi_tracepoints`, `lookup_kapi_modules`, `lookup_kapi_devices`, `search_mail`, `get_mail_message`, `get_mail_thread`, `get_mail_merged_commits`, `get_stable_backport_gaps`, `get_subsystem_health`, `get_release_cve_report`, `check_watched_changes`, `lookup_maintainers`, `match_patch_maintainers`, `get_maintainer_person`, `preview_nodemap_canvas`, `create_nodemap_canvas`, ...); `title` is the `_ENDPOINT_CATALOG` summary; `description` is the handler docstring plus any required repository feature (`Requires \`<feature>\` repository feature.`).
- **Input schema**: each route's `Path`, `Query`, and Pydantic body model fields are merged into one flat pydantic model (`extra="forbid"`) whose JSON Schema is the tool's `inputSchema`: `type`, `default`, `minimum`/`maximum` (`ge`/`le`), `minLength`/`maxLength`, `minItems`, `pattern`, `enum`, `required`, and `additionalProperties: false`. Nested Pydantic `$defs`/`$ref` pointers are recursively dereferenced inline so no `$ref` or `$defs` appear in `inputSchema`. Optional `str | None` parameters appear as their plain type without a `null` default. Query and body aliases are the argument names (`get_callpath` and `check_watched_changes` take `from` and `to`; the Python names `src`/`dst` and `from_rev`/`to_rev` validate too). Duplicate REST convenience aliases (`_MCP_OMITTED_PARAMS`, e.g., `a`/`b` vs `version_a`/`version_b`, `struct` vs `name`, `patch` vs `patch_text`, `touched_files` vs `paths`, `email` vs `person_id_or_email`, `from_file` vs `current_file`, `page` vs `offset`, `expand`/`layout`/`upsert_tour` on NodeMap tools) are omitted from MCP `inputSchema` while remaining accepted on `/api/v1/*` REST endpoints. NodeMap authoring inputs (`NodemapNodeInput`, `NodemapEdgeInput`, `NodemapGroupInput`, `NodemapTourInput`) expose explicit nested `properties` and `enum` constraints for all 16 `NODE_TYPES`, `nodes[].data`, `edges[]`, `groups[]`, and `tours[]`. Every tool also takes an optional `repo` string (`minLength: 1`, `maxLength: 128`).
- **Read-only POST tools, write-scope visibility & annotations**: read-only tools (all MCP-enabled `GET` routes plus the stateless read-only `POST` tools `preview_nodemap_canvas`, `match_patch_maintainers`, and `check_watched_changes`) have `required_scope=None`, carry `{"readOnlyHint": true, "destructiveHint": false, "idempotentHint": true, "openWorldHint": false}`, and remain visible in `tools/list` and callable via `tools/call` even when `api.allow_writes` is `False`. Write-scoped tools (`required_scope="nodemap:write"`) carry `readOnlyHint: false`, `destructiveHint: true` on `delete_nodemap_canvas` (`false` otherwise), and `idempotentHint: true` on `replace_nodemap_canvas`, `delete_nodemap_canvas`, and `layout_nodemap_canvas`. `visible_tools()` hides write-scoped tools from `tools/list` whenever `api.allow_writes` is `False` or the caller lacks `required_scope`, and `tools/call` enforces `require_write_scope` (`403`).
- **REST-only opt-out (`mcp=False`)**: `_ENDPOINT_CATALOG` entries with `"mcp": False` (`GET /api/v1/compile_commands`, `GET /api/v1/treemap`, `POST /api/v1/checkpatch`) are skipped by `build_tool_registry()`, omitted from `TOOLS` and `tools/list`, and rejected with `-32602` (`INVALID_PARAMS`) on `tools/call`.
- **Validation**: arguments validate before the handler runs, with query-string-like scalar coercion (`"10"` → `10`, `"true"` → `true`); a bare string for a `list[str]` parameter (`grep_code.path`, `eval_kconfig.symbol`, `lookup_maintainers.path`, ...) counts as a one-item list on both `param.alias` and `param.name`. NodeMap canvas calls (`preview_nodemap_canvas`, `create_nodemap_canvas`, `replace_nodemap_canvas`, `mutate_nodemap_canvas`) run `validate_nodemap_payload_strict()` across `nodes[]`, `edges[]`, `groups[]`, `tours[]`, `ops[]`, and `canvas`, rejecting unknown node types, misplaced top-level fields outside `data`, invalid `data` keys for the node's `type`, and malformed `groups[]`/`tours[]` with `isError: true` (`422`) and an actionable message naming the offending path and expected schema.
- **Compact MCP projections & opt-in flags**: `_project_mcp_result()` keeps MCP responses compact while leaving `/api/v1/*` REST defaults unchanged:
  - `get_capabilities`: defaults `include_endpoints=false` on MCP (omitting `endpoints[]` unless `include_endpoints=true` or `verbose=true`) and reports session-accurate `read_only`, `scopes`, and `mcp.tools` (`len(visible_tools())`).
  - `preview_nodemap_canvas`: emits a single canonical `export` field (omitting duplicate `export_content`), defaults `include_canvas` to `false` when `export_format` is set (`true` otherwise), and strips empty/default UI-state keys (`color`, `bgColor`, `customTitle`, `locks`, `collapsed`, `hiddenItems`, `fieldLocks`, `openMids`, `fullMids`, `pinnedBodies`, `waypoints`, `typeOverrides`, `collapsedGuards`) unless `verbose=true`.
  - `get_nodemap_canvas`, `attach_nested_nodemap`, `group_nodemap_nodes` (and `nested_maps` in the other canvas write results): each `nested_maps[*].preview` is reduced to `{w, h, boxes, segments, truncated}` counts (coordinate arrays dropped) while `status`, `name`, `counts`, `revision`, and `webapp_url` stay; `verbose=true` keeps the full geometry. Nested node `data.canvasId` stays in `canvas.nodes` so agents drill down with `get_nodemap_canvas` / `get_nodemap_hierarchy`.
  - `get_mail_message`: defaults `include_raw=false` (omits `raw`) and `include_headers="essential"` (retaining `from`, `to`, `cc`, `date`, `subject`, `message-id`, `in-reply-to`, `references`, omitting transport/auth headers), and omits duplicate `commit_message == body` and `review_trailers == trailers` unless `verbose=true`.
  - `get_kconfig_symbol`: deduplicates repeated `help`, `prompt`/`prompts`, `declarations`, and `compiled_files` covered by `kbuild` unless `verbose=true`.
  - `get_nodemap_struct`, `get_struct_layout`, and `get_tree`: omit null, `false`, `0`-default, empty-collection, and internal (`fid`, `ftype`, `s_stat`, `e_stat`, `s_stat_label`) per-item defaults unless `verbose=true`.
- **Execution**: `call_tool()` selects the repository (`repo` argument, else the transport default), runs the route's feature and write-scope dependencies (`require_feature`, `require_write_scope`), instantiates any Pydantic request body model, and calls the `api/routers/` handler in-process, so behaviour, limits, and responses equal the REST endpoint. `set_active_repository()` / `reset_active_repository()` wrap each call in `try`/`finally`; overrides never outlive the call.
- **Results**: success returns `content: [{"type": "text", "text": <compact JSON>}]`, `structuredContent` (the handler's JSON object; non-objects nest under `result`), and `isError: false`. A `job_answer()` `202` building state (`get_callpath`, `get_implementations`, KAPI/Kbuild/Insights jobs) is a success whose payload has `state: "building"` and `retry_after_ms`.
- **Tool errors** (`isError: true`, `structuredContent: {"error": {"status", "detail"}}`, text `HTTP <status>: <detail>`): argument validation failures (`422`, `detail` lists `loc` / `msg` / `type`), a blank `repo` (`422`), an unknown `repo` (`404`), handler `HTTPException`s (`400` invalid input, `403` disabled feature or missing write scope, `404`, `409` revision conflict, `500` failed job), degraded mail archive responses (`search_mail`, `get_mail_message`, and `get_mail_thread` payloads with `available: false` or a non-empty `error` field, which set `isError: true`), and unexpected handler exceptions (`500`, `"Internal server error"`, traceback only in the log).
- **Protocol errors** (`-32602`): unknown tool names, a missing `name`, and non-object `arguments` (omitted `arguments` means `{}`).

### 5.3 Streamable HTTP Transport (`/api/mcp`)

`create_app()` always mounts `api/mcp.py` `router` beside `v1_router`, behind the same middleware stack (§3): `ApiAuthMiddleware` (API key, key scopes, progressive IP lockout, per-key and per-IP rate limits shared with `/api/v1/*`; a batch counts as one request and runs at most one tool), `ApiRequestLoggingMiddleware`, `SecurityHeadersMiddleware`, `RepoContextMiddleware` (`X-KI-Repo` / `?repo=` set the default repository of every call in the request), and `GZipMiddleware`. No CORS middleware is added and the routes are excluded from `/api/openapi.json`. The Anubis `/api/*` bypass (§6) covers `/api/mcp`.

- `POST /api/mcp`: body of at most `MAX_BODY_BYTES` (1 MiB, else `413`). Requests answer `200` with `application/json` (a JSON-RPC response or batch array); notification-only bodies answer `202` with an empty body; malformed JSON (`-32700`) and envelope errors without a usable `id` (`-32600`) answer `400`. An `MCP-Protocol-Version` header outside `SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS` answers `400`. Dispatch runs in the threadpool (`run_in_threadpool`), which copies the request's `ContextVar` repository and key-scope state.
- `GET`, `DELETE`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS /api/mcp`: `405` with `Allow: POST` (no SSE stream, no sessions to terminate).

### 5.4 stdio Transport (`api/mcp_stdio.py`)

`python3 api/mcp_stdio.py [-c config.json] [--repo NAME] [--allow-writes]` reads newline-delimited JSON-RPC messages from stdin (blank lines skipped; a raw line over `MAX_BODY_BYTES` before whitespace stripping is `-32600` and its remainder is discarded), answers each request with one compact JSON line on stdout, and processes messages sequentially until EOF. `claim_stdout()` duplicates file descriptor 1 for frames, then points fd 1 and `sys.stdout` at stderr before configuration loads, so logs, `print()`, warnings, and child processes never reach the frame stream; `setup_api_logging(capture_stdio=False)` keeps configured `logging.api` file logs. `--repo` sets the session's default repository (an unknown name exits with status `2`). Passing `--allow-writes` binds a session override via `set_allow_writes_override(True)` (`api/config.py`) that explicitly enables writes for that stdio session even when `API_ALLOW_WRITES=0` or `KIP_API_ALLOW_WRITES=0` is set in the environment, and grants `frozenset({"read", "nodemap:write"})` (restoring both the override and scopes on exit); when `--allow-writes` is not passed, `serve()` honors the effective env/config `api.allow_writes` setting (defaulting to `frozenset({"read"})`). EOF, `SIGINT`, and `SIGTERM` all run the shutdown path. Startup and shutdown reuse `api/app.py` `startup_resources()` (DB pool warm-up) and `shutdown_resources()` (job cancellation, DB engine shutdown, database SSH tunnel stop), exactly like the HTTP lifespan. stdio has no API key: it trusts the local process owner.

### 5.5 Client Configuration

Streamable HTTP (Claude Code; any `Authorization: Bearer` or `X-API-Key` header works):

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http kernelinfo https://kernel.example.org/api/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $KIP_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kernelinfo": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/mcp",
      "headers": { "X-API-Key": "<api key>", "X-KI-Repo": "linux" }
    }
  }
}
```

Local stdio (Claude Desktop `claude_desktop_config.json`, Claude Code `.mcp.json`, or `claude mcp add kernelinfo -- python3 /path/to/KernelInfo-Parser/api/mcp_stdio.py -c /path/to/config_api.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kernelinfo": {
      "command": "python3",
      "args": ["/path/to/KernelInfo-Parser/api/mcp_stdio.py", "-c", "/path/to/config_api.json", "--repo", "linux"]
    }
  }
}
```

Remote OAuth 2.1 Streamable HTTP (`api.oauth.enabled: true`, URL `https://kernelinfo.org/api/mcp`):

- **Claude.ai / Claude Desktop / Claude Code**:
  - In Claude.ai / Claude Desktop (*Settings -> Connectors -> Add custom connector*), set Remote MCP Server URL to `https://kernelinfo.org/api/mcp` (uses CIMD or DCR automatically; enter your server API key on the consent page).
  - In Claude Code CLI: `claude mcp add --transport http kernelinfo https://kernelinfo.org/api/mcp` and run `/mcp` to complete browser OAuth consent.
- **ChatGPT (Connectors / Deep Research / Developer Mode)**:
  - In *Settings -> Connectors -> Create*, set MCP Server URL to `https://kernelinfo.org/api/mcp` with Authentication set to *OAuth* (discovers `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and registers or presents CIMD automatically).
- **Gemini Web App / Gemini CLI / Antigravity**:
  - For Gemini CLI or Antigravity `.mcp.json`, configure `{"mcpServers": {"kernelinfo": {"url": "https://kernelinfo.org/api/mcp"}}}` (or pre-register a client in `api.oauth.clients` when configuring a static client ID/secret in Google Workspace / Gemini extensions).
- **Cursor / VS Code / GitHub Copilot**:
  - Set server `url` to `https://kernelinfo.org/api/mcp` in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`; the IDE follows the `401 WWW-Authenticate` challenge, registers a loopback/custom-scheme callback via DCR, and opens the consent page in the browser.

## 6. Operations: Systemd, TUI Launch & Reverse Proxy

- **Systemd**: `core/systemd_manager.py` manages `kernelinfo-api.service` (`API_SERVICE_NAME = "kernelinfo-api"`, `API_UNIT_NAME`) beside the daemon and webapp units (`VALID_SERVICES = ("daemon", "webapp", "api")`). `ExecStart` runs `python3 api/main.py --config <config_api.json>` directly (`Type=simple`) or inside tmux (`Type=forking`, socket and session `kernelinfo-api`). Preflight warns when the configuration has no `api` section or no `api.keys` (every request would answer `401`).
- **Configuration TUI** (`core/API.md` §7.3): `ScopedConfigMenuScreen("api")` edits `config_api.json` (`ApiSettingsScreen` in `core/tui/screens/api_cfg.py`: server, `allow_writes`, `nodemap_canvas_dir`, masked keys with per-key scopes, limits, trusted proxies, client-IP header, and the `OAuth` tab for `api.oauth.enabled`, `issuer`, `allow_dcr`, `allow_cimd`, `data_dir`, and masked pre-registered `clients`; `LoggingScreen` for `logging.api`), and `SystemdServicesScreen` installs and controls the API unit.
- **Foreground launch**: main-menu item `W` (`Launch Webapp / API Servers`) asks for *Webapp only*, *API only*, or *Both*, resolves unsaved edits with `choose_launch_config()`, and exits the TUI with `{"servers": [...], "config_path": ...}`. `pipeline/cli.py` `arg_handling()` hands that to `launch_servers()` before the parser's memory guard and logging: each server runs as `python3 <entry> -c <config>` in its own process group; SIGINT/SIGTERM are forwarded to every server, one server exiting stops the others, and a server still running 15 s (`SERVER_STOP_GRACE_SECONDS`) after the stop signal is killed.
- **Reverse proxy & Anubis**: route `/.well-known/oauth-*`, `/.well-known/openid-configuration`, and `/api/*` (including `/api/mcp` and `/api/oauth/*`) around Anubis directly to the API port (`8001`) and everything else (`/`, `/b/*`, `/static/*`, `/webapi/*`, `/sw.js`, `/manifest.json`) through Anubis to the webapp port (`8000`). The proxy must reach the API from an address in `api.trusted_proxies` and set `api.client_ip_header` (overwriting, not appending to, any client-supplied `X-Real-IP` / `CF-Connecting-IP`; appending to `X-Forwarded-For` is safe because hops are read right-to-left). Without a trusted proxy hop, lockout and rate limits key on the socket peer, so a proxy outside `trusted_proxies` would make every client share its address.

Example Nginx reverse-proxy configuration bypassing Anubis for OAuth 2.1 discovery and `/api/`:

```nginx
# OAuth 2.1 / OIDC discovery metadata -> standalone AI API service (port 8001, bypasses Anubis)
location ~ ^/\.well-known/(oauth-protected-resource|oauth-authorization-server|openid-configuration)(/.*)?$ {
    proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8001;
    proxy_http_version 1.1;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Host $host;
}

# Authenticated REST API (/api/v1/*), MCP (/api/mcp), and OAuth endpoints (/api/oauth/*) -> port 8001
location /api/ {
    proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8001;
    proxy_http_version 1.1;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Host $host;
    proxy_buffering off;
}
```
